stories.description:
Jadis has no idea how she died. One minute she's living her life as a young college student in Pennsylvania, the next she's hurtling through the unimaginable, incomprehensible void of the space between realities as a lost and detached soul. Luckily for her, the bored, and slightly deranged, god D finds her soul before it is mulched by the incomprehensible cosmos. After offering her a cookie to calm down from her existential nightmare, he explains that not only are gods and their respective afterlives real, but her disbelief in gods while living also means she doesn’t qualify to enter any god’s afterlife upon death. However, since D is in the mood for some mischief, he strikes a deal with her. Life in a fantasy world with RPG elements, along with a body built to match Jadis' slightly perverted wishes. Additionally, she gets a guaranteed spot in his afterlife. All that for the low price of spicing up the stagnant cyclical nature of a never-ending war between two stubborn gods and their respective followers on said magic-filled world. What disembodied soul could turn down an offer like that?

Except, once Jadis takes the deal, she finds that she has been transported to the middle of nowhere and the lazy jerk of a god forgot to check if any of his followers were around to greet Jadis. Now freshly reincarnated as a Nephilim, Jadis is all alone and all but naked in an abandoned dwarven village located firmly in demon infested territory. Not planning on dying again anytime soon, she is forced to take the only non-perverted class option given to her and unexpectedly receives a second body for it. How is Jadis going to explain that when she gets back to civilization? From there, the now pluralized Jadis tries to survive long enough to understand her new system and skills, looking forward to the day she finds civilization, hot baths, and hotter elves.

[Story will be updated on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. Double chapter release every Friday. I'll try to keep the chapters consistent in length, but some will be longer or shorter than others.]

[Now cross-posting on Royal Road]

reviews.title: chapter 143: the whole truth
reviews.content:
Nothing at first glance does this story justice. It is an example of taking a tried and true template and using it to make an exceptionally good story. There are some portions where it feels like a wall of text for me, however, that just may be adult life and my lack of sleep catching up. I won't tell you if you'll like it or not, but I will tell you what to expect.

First— the grammar. Is. Perfect. The story flows well and it is easy to follow the story as you go along (which says a lot, coming from someone with a severe lack of sleep and concentration). I don't recall any spelling or grammatical mistakes, which says a lot, because it means I rode the boat so smoothly I either didn't notice it or was too engrossed to care. There is also a good, conscientious use of those box/table/cell thingies to make the system and notifications pop out.

Second— the characters. Our main character is Jadis (Jey-Diss). She, for some reason, died, and we catch her in the rift between worlds, watching the cosmos and going insane from the utter scale of that which was not meant for mortal eyes, just there, until she wasn't. She then finds herself in a place that can only be described as the very essence of a living room facing a figure that can only be described as the very essence of an anthropomorphic figure. The god, D (Dee), explains that not only are gods and their respective afterlives real, and that in her disbelief of gods (or lack of anyone capable of proving otherwise), Jadis does not qualify to enter anygod's afterlife upon death, but that she, Jadis, is well and, well... dead. Which means back to cosmic existential crises. Unless— that is, Jadis can accomplish D's quest for her. D seeks chaos, a fresh change in a stalemate of a war on one of his worlds. In exchange, D offers, for one, to not throw Jadis back into the void, even better, he will make a new body for her, custom built according to her deepest, darkest desires. Should Jadis accomplish D's quest, Jadis will be given a second chance to live the life she's always wanted to live, on a world full of magic and adventure (and hot elves), plus, a sweet spot reserved for her in D's afterlife. Jadis, obviously, accepts, lest the story end right there, and is rickrolled by D in the middle of nowhere, leaving her to figure out how to survive the night— and the demon spawn of Samleos he courteously deigned to not inform Jadis about. From there, Jadis (plural) tries (emphasis on "tries") to understand her new system and skills, looking forward to the day she finds civilization, hot baths, and hotter elves. The love interests:

Aila (Ay-La) - I swear I keep misreading her name as Alia. Our poor cart driver really wants to be a mage and our MC would love to help with that, especially since Aila is tall, legs, and thighs, nuff said (—Jadis, probably)

Eir (E-Ir) - Cinnamon bun healer, sheltered, protected, succubus in nun clothing, and, according to Jadis, schmexy. She is a devotee of Lyssandria, and a big fan of the Nephilim, and all that goes under 1 (three) particular Nephilim.

Thea (They-Ya) - Nervous bundle of introverted cuteness. Surprisingly schmexy, according to Jadis, and a drop dead beauty when she's not trying to socialize or stand next to Eir.

Kerr (Ke-Grrrrrr) - Beast people! Horns! Ears! Fluffy tail! Drunk huntress? Nuff said. The exact opposite of Thea, outgoing and not afraid to get dirty... in more ways than one.

Special Guard Captain Ealdread - Technically not a love interest. Still, he's a gigachad. I press F for respect. ;o;7

Third— the plot. Yeah, just read above, it's already there lmao. The plot is understandable, and there are simple plot twists that you will either feel good seeing coming or be genuinely surprised when it hits. The progression is fine and doesn't leave you wondering what the heck is happening.

Finally— the world building! It's well thought out, and the world makes sense from the standpoint it's supposed to make sense from. Now for the real final point— the smut.

Expect a lot of self love and "definitely masturbation" at first. Until our MC finds civilization, only then will the real fun start *wink wink*

reviews.title: chapter 422
reviews.content:
I expected to enjoy this as 3/5 popcorn thing, or a smut story I'd drop after a dozen or so chapters.

Unfortunately, that wasn't enough for the author. This is one of the better LitRPG stories I've read. Probably top 5/10 for me at least.

The futa/s*x aspect is prominent, but also incredibly story driven. Does the MC love s*x and have it often and with gusto? Yes. However, the s*x scenes aren't thrown in every other chapter which is good and they contribute to the story in a way that's rare.

Everything about this is well written and thought out. The world building, character arcs and action scenes. Even the day to day "mundane" scenes are fantastic.

This is truly top notch. If you don't enjoy stories with s*x scenes, you probably won't enjoy it but if you are even neutral on the idea I'd wager you'll enjoy this.

My only complaint is that I caught up and finished reading it

reviews.title: chapter 435: romantic
reviews.content:
This here is what every smut novel should strive for, having a plot so good and fluid that it outshines even the stellar smut.

I was stacking since chapter 216 and finally decided to catch back up to the current chapter. I also created an account for this site just to review this amazing novel. You must give it a read. The plot flows wonderfully where even mundane SoL chapters add to the story. Every single side character, especially the harem members, are unique with their own amazing personalities. Very good power system that is easy to follow; some fans also created a google doc spreadsheet for easy reference. Smut mostly revolves around harem orgies featuring futanari as probably the biggest kink. So that would be the only "negative" factor to not read this novel, I know some hate harems and futanari (not me).

For the technical side of things, I don't think I've seen a single grammar or spelling error in my 435 chapters of reading. The novel is very easy to understand but also has a ton of depth with the language used.

Now comes the hardest choice, stacking chapters for another half-full year again, or read once they immediately drop. Decisions decisions...
